newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian doctor says Tudjman "feeling excellent".
newsitem.headline: Croatian doctor says Tudjman "feeling excellent".

text.p: Croatian President Franjo Tudjman is "feeling excellent" and is still able to discharge his duties despite his illness, one of the leader's doctors said on Saturday.
Tudjman was admitted to Walter Reed Hospital in Washington earlier this week and American officials said he was seriously ill.
"Since therapy was applied, the disorders have been subsiding," hematologist Branimir Jaksic told state TV by telephone from Washington.
The Croatian doctor made no mention of reports from U.S. officials that Tudjman had stomach cancer.

Croatian government officials, apparently anxious to discourage speculation about the 74-year-old president's health, have avoided any mention of cancer and described his illness merely as a "digestion problem".
Jaksic said the disorder was diagnosed as having been caused by a stomach ulcer.

"There is no ground for conjectures that there is a problem which would reduce (the president's) working ability, and certainly not a state that would require his prolonged absence from work in the next few months," he said.

Confirming earlier reports from state media, Jaksic said Tudjman would be returning to Croatia next week and added that he had asked his regular tennis partners for a match at the usual time next Sunday.

The TV reported that the head of the Croatian Catholic Church, Archbishop Franjo Kuharic, had sent the president his blessings through the Croatian embassy in Washington and was praying for his speedy recovery.
Political analysts say there is no clear heir to Tudjman, who is regarded as "father of the nation," and predict a power struggle if the president fails to recover from his illness.
